name: Ladis
kurzbeschreibung: Exclusive mountain village on the high plateau – part of Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis with top-tier hotels and pristine air.
beschreibung:
Overview

Ladis is an enchanting alpine village in the Tyrolean Oberinntal, forming the celebrated holiday plateau of Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis alongside its neighbours. Perched at an elevation of 1,189 metres on a sun-drenched terrace high above the Inn Valley at the base of the Samnaun Alps, the municipality is home to roughly 550 residents. Ladis has carefully preserved its authentic Rhaeto-Romanic charm, distinguished by listed timber-and-stone farmsteads adorned with intricate frescoes and peaceful winding lanes. High above the village, medieval Castle Laudeck crowns a dramatic slate crag overlooking the castle reflection pond. In addition to historic healing springs, Ladis offers seamless access to one of the premier family ski arenas in Europe.

History

Traces of human settlement on the castle rock date back to the Bronze Age and Roman antiquity, when travelers traversed the Via Claudia Augusta. In 1212, a shepherd discovered mineral-rich effervescent springs, establishing Obladis as Tyrol's oldest documented medicinal spa. Around 1200, the Bishops of Brixen erected Castle Laudeck, which later fell to the Counts of Tyrol and served as the administrative seat for regional high courts until the 16th century. Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I famously prized the mineral waters of Obladis for his health retreats. Following a major fire in 1634, grand homesteads were rebuilt in the Engadine architectural style featuring ornate trompe-l'œil facade paintings, most notably exemplified by the historic Rechelerhaus.

Getting There

Ladis enjoys straightforward accessibility throughout the year. Motorists travel via the A12 Inntal Autobahn and S16 Arlberg Expressway, exiting towards Ried im Oberinntal before following the well-paved L19 scenic mountain road up to the sunny plateau. Train passengers arrive at the Landeck-Zams railway hub, which accommodates international EuroCity and Railjet connections. Frequent public regional buses operated by VVT run directly from Landeck via Ried to Ladis. A dedicated regional shuttle and ski bus network connects Ladis effortlessly with Fiss and Serfaus.

Tips

A leisurely walk around the idyllic castle pond with reflections of Castle Laudeck provides one of Western Tyrol's most striking photographic panoramas. Visitors should taste the natural effervescent mineral water at the historic Sauerbrunn pavilion, which flows fresh from the mountain spring. In winter, the Sonnenbahn cable car whisks winter sports enthusiasts directly into the Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis ski domain, featuring 214 kilometres of slopes and scenic descents like the Frommes run. In summer, the interactive Explorers' Trail delivers an engaging outdoor experience for families discovering alpine nature.
